findings.summary: Stale-armed reproduction must be an explicit AC, not Open Question. Operator's bug may persist after narrowing if deriveListenerState() returns stale 'armed' post-sync-review-mail.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Promote stale-armed handling to a hard AC (new AC-9): 'After a synchronous review-mail call mutates the manifest, deriveListenerState() must return non-armed when the listener process is dead, even if heartbeat was just touched.' Add a test fixture that seeds post-review-mail manifest state with stale-armed AND verifies that decideStopBlock returns a block. If actor-state hardening is required, fold it into US-001.
findings.resolution: Promoted the post-review-mail stale-armed reproduction into AC-9, added required stop-decision coverage, made actor-state hardening in-scope for US-001, and removed it from Open Questions.

The LISTENER_REL_PATH constant at hooks/paths.js:28 also references 'wait-for-message.js' — assess whether that needs to change too (it points to the file that still exists for shim purposes; likely NO change needed, but document).

findings.summary: Version-bump scope incomplete. bump-version.js touches 6 files, not 5. tests/version.test.js has a pinned 'const VERSION = 1.6.0' that the script rewrites (lines 65-72 of bump-version.js).
findings.suggestedAmendment: Add tests/version.test.js to the list of files touched by bump-version.js. Update the Out-of-Scope note that incorrectly claims 'tests/version.test.js auto-passes' — it is auto-rewritten, not auto-passed.
findings.resolution: Added tests/version.test.js to the bump-version plan scope and clarified that bump-version.js rewrites its pinned VERSION literal.

findings.summary: AC-1 wording 'containing the exact arm command' does not explicitly state that <name> is positional. Without this clarification, an implementer may add --name flag support to listener-loop.js instead of swapping the command form. Spec literally says '--name <name>' which is misleading.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Rewrite AC-1 to explicitly call out the exact command literal: 'node <plugin>/tools/crews.js arm <name> --crew <crew> --cwd <cwd> --session-id <session-id> where <name> is POSITIONAL (NOT --name <name>). The arm subcommand parser in lib/listener-loop.js does not declare a --name flag. Spec example is informal and inaccurate.'
findings.resolution: Clarified AC-1 to require the exact positional `crews.js arm <name>` command literal and note that `--name` is not supported by the parser.

findings.summary: Plan claims CREWS_REVIEW_MODE=off disables BOTH the review-required AND listener-armed gates. This is incorrect: hooks/stop.js only consults reviewMode around the review-required block (lines 602-614); the listener-armed gate runs later regardless of CREWS_REVIEW_MODE.
findings.location: draft-plan.md Out of Scope ('existing CREWS_REVIEW_MODE=off knob already disables both...')
findings.suggestedAmendment: Remove the inaccurate claim. State accurately: 'No new env-var knob is added. CREWS_REVIEW_MODE=off disables ONLY the review-required gate (not the listener-armed gate). If a debug-bypass knob for the listener-armed gate is desired, it requires its own env var — defer to a follow-up task.'

findings.summary: Ordering: findPendingConsumedEntries() runs at stop.js:710, AFTER decideStopBlock() at stop.js:654. To use unresolved.length for queueDepth in the gate, code must be reordered OR the computation duplicated.
findings.location: draft-plan.md Implementation Strategy; US-001 acceptance criteria
findings.suggestedAmendment: Add explicit subtask in US-001: 'reorder or extract the findPendingConsumedEntries() + evaluateConsumedResolutions() computation to run BEFORE decideStopBlock(), or pass the count into decideStopBlock() as a parameter.' Note in Risk #7 that the reorder must preserve the existing strict-ack behavior at stop.js:710-734.

findings.summary: AC-4 fixtures may not be constructible with current stop-decision.test.js harness if it can only inject manifest fields (not inbox-history mailbox entries). Without realistic mailbox state, queueDepth=0 cannot be tested distinctly from kind-only gating.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Clarify AC-4: 'Fixtures must construct realistic inbox-history state via mailbox helpers (e.g., appendInboxHistory, consumeMailbox) to verify queueDepth derivation. If cfg.ensureActorDir cannot wire up inbox-history, the fixture must call the lower-level helpers directly. Document the fixture-setup helper in the test comment.'

findings.summary: Missing risk on in-turn queueDepth staleness. If findPendingConsumedEntries() is called naively without first computing same-turn resolutions, progress turns that resolved consumed entries via current <|report|> tags will be over-blocked.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Add Risk #8: 'Stale queueDepth in same-turn resolutions. The new gate MUST call evaluateConsumedResolutions() FIRST and use resolution.unresolved.length as queueDepth — not the raw findPendingConsumedEntries().length. Mitigation: reuse the existing computation at stop.js:711 (move it earlier or duplicate-cheap).'

findings.summary: AC-6 ('cross-plugin coexistence') is asserted as 'structurally guaranteed' but has no verification path. Either add a fixture or drop AC-6.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Either (a) add a fixture that runs the Stop hook in a workspace where another plugin's hook directory exists and asserts no spurious block, OR (b) demote AC-6 from acceptance criterion to documentation note in Out-of-Scope ('agent-peers has no Stop hook; no cross-plugin coexistence verification needed').

findings.summary: AC-2 wording 'passes the Stop hook without listener-state check' is hard to observe. The check is internal; from outside, you can only observe whether a block was emitted.
findings.suggestedAmendment: Reframe AC-2 as observable behavior: 'A turn ending with kind=progress AND zero unresolved consumed entries (queueDepth=0) does NOT produce a JSON block on stdout with a reason mentioning listener/arm — the Stop hook exits without emitting any block (or emits a block for unrelated reasons only).'
